text:
Anna W: Heads up — canary deploy for payments-service chart v2.4.1 failed preflight on eu-prod canary. deploy-bot shows RELEASE_SUCCEEDED then post-install hook job crashed with BackoffLimitExceeded. Not sure if this is a chart hook bug or infra SIGTERM. Need rollback plan and release-notes callout. :eyes:

deploy-bot: helm upgrade --install payments-service charts/payments --namespace prod --set image.tag=release-2026-03-20
```
RELEASE_STATUS: SUCCESS
HOOK: post-install-job payments-migrate-job
JOB_STATUS: BackoffLimitExceeded
kubectl describe job payments-migrate-job-1647
  Last Termination: SIGTERM
```

Mike L: Seen the same on us-west canary about 5 mins apart. Not widespread yet but repeating across canaries.

Sarah P: I think the migration job uses restartPolicy: Never and heavy memory. Could be OOMKilled then kubelet SIGTERM. Diego, can you grab pod events/logs?

Diego R: logs look like this:
```
I0319 12:01:11.123456 1 main.go:88] starting migrate
Killed
```
No oom message in container logs, but node kubelet logs show eviction SIGTERM around same time.

Jordan K: Proposed immediate plan:
- Rollback canary to chart v2.4.0 (pin canary image/tag) to stop further noise.
- Create chart patch v2.4.2 that changes hook to run as a Job with activeDeadlineSeconds + restartPolicy OnFailure and reduces memory requests temporarily.
- Add values flag `preflight.enabled=false` for fast rollback option.
- Update release notes: call out migration job behavior and recommended post-deploy manual run for large clusters.

Anna W: +1. Can we avoid a full hotfix release if we can patch hook behavior in-place? Or safer to release v2.4.2 and run a controlled rollout outside change window? We need to communicate to SRE and Support.

Mike L: I'll open a chart PR with the `preflight.enabled` flag and a canary pinning patch. Will also add a short changelog fragment for release notes: "Fix: migration job stability on high-memory nodes (opt-in change)".

Sarah P: If we pin the canary, we should also create a quick smoke test that exercises the migration job without changing prod DB — maybe use a replica DB or a dry-run flag.

Diego R: For immediate rollback, run:
```
helm rollback payments-service 23 --namespace prod
kubectl patch deployment payments --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"rollback-at":"1977777777"}}}}}'
```
That rollback command will revert release to 2.4.0. I'll monitor nodes for eviction pressure.

deploy-bot: Rollback executed by Mike L: helm rollback payments-service 23 -> deployed release v2.4.0 (canary). Health checks starting. :white_check_mark:

Anna W: Thanks — please update the release-notes PR with the migration note and the rollback timeline (include failed job logs snippet). Also add an action for SRE to investigate node eviction cause.

Mike L: Will do. Opening PR now and tagging @sre. Adding a changelog and notes for on-call. :thumbsup:

Jordan K: Follow-ups: create v2.4.2 branch, add memory request tweak, change hook to OnFailure, add preflight.enabled default true, and plan rollout in the next maintenance window. I’ll own the rollout playbook.

Sarah P: Filing a support blurb to customer-facing release notes: short note that customers on large clusters may see delayed migration runs and to contact support if they have migration-critical workloads.

Anna W: Good. Keep updates here. If rollback shows any residual flakes we pause all canaries and escalate.

Mike L: Update — canary health checks passed after rollback, metrics look stable for 3 mins. Will hold for 20 mins then proceed with chart patch PR review.

Diego R: I'm collecting node pressure metrics and will post a short summary in #eng-sre.

deploy-bot: Note: automated release notes draft created at https://internal/release-notes/payments/2.4.2-draft. Use PR #4521 for edits.

Anna W: Perfect. Closing loop here — thanks everyone.
